The School Everyone Is Talking About
WELCOME TO RADNOR HOUSE Where every student thrives in a supportive community dedicated to excellence in education and personal growth. Our commitment to nurturing each individual and fostering a strong sense of community shapes every aspect of our school.
Integral values
OUR VALUES-LED APPROACH to education fosters a caring, happy and ambitious community with a global outlook, enhanced by our membership of the RoundSquare group of international schools.

Excellence
WE COMMIT TO GIVING our best effort in every moment because every second counts. We cherish excellence across our school community, fostering an environment where everyone is encouraged to strive for their personal best. We celebrate both individual accomplishments and collective achievements, recognising and honouring the diverse talents and successes of all our students.
Respect
RESPECT IS FOUNDATIONAL to our community, recognising that success in life hinges on nurturing strong relationships. We foster self-respect among staff and students, emphasising their inherent value and importance. Additionally, we cultivate respect for others, embracing both similarities and differences.
Courage
COURAGE AT RADNOR House Sevenoaks extends beyond bravery; it embodies the courage to make principled choices over convenient ones. We encourage students to take risks, make mistakes, and learn from failures, understanding that these experiences are crucial aspects of the learning process.
Perseverance
WE ENCOURAGE students to sustain their interest and effort to achieve their goals, even in the face of challenges. Emphasising patience and the understanding that worthwhile achievements take time, we instil a commitment to seeing tasks through to completion and finishing them with excellence.

90% of the Brain Develops Before Five: Why the Early Years Matter More Than Ever | Blog | Radnor House Sevenoaks | Private School in Kent
90% of the Brain Develops Before Five: Why the Early Years Matter More Than Ever
It’s a striking statistic: by the age of five, around 90% of a child’s brain development has already taken place.
Long before formal lessons or exams, the foundations for learning, behaviour and wellbeing are already being laid - quietly, powerfully, and often invisibly.
This growing understanding is increasingly reflected in national focus on early childhood, including the work of Catherine, Princess of Wales and The Royal Foundation Centre for Early Childhood. Her work brings to the forefront a simple but profound idea: the experiences of the first five years shape not only how children learn, but who they become.
More Than Preparation: A Period of Formation
The first five years represent a period of extraordinary growth. During this time, children are not simply acquiring skills—they are building the architecture of the brain itself. Research consistently shows that early experiences shape how children:
Dr Jack Shonkoff of Harvard University describes this stage as one in which the brain is built through everyday interactions, underlining the importance of responsive, engaged care. These are not optional advantages - they are the foundations of future academic success and personal confidence. Before a child picks up a pencil, they are already learning how to learn.
The Skills That Can’t Be Taught Later
When we think about education, we often focus on reading, writing and numeracy. Yet some of the most important skills developed in the early years are less visible - and far more enduring.
In a high-quality early years environment, children develop:
Often described as the “invisible curriculum”, these skills underpin all future learning. As highlighted in national conversations such as the Princess of Wales’s Shaping Us campaign, social and emotional development is not secondary - it enables academic success.
It is not simply attending a nursery or pre-school that makes the difference - it is the quality of the experience.
Research led by Professor Kathy Sylva, through the landmark Effective Provision of Pre-School Education (EPPSE) study, has shown that children who attend high-quality early years settings benefit not only in the short term, but throughout their educational journey. These children demonstrate stronger academic outcomes, greater social confidence and improved long-term prospects, with the effects still visible well into secondary school. Crucially, the research highlights that early education is most impactful when it is thoughtfully structured, with a clear focus on both cognitive and social development.
Quality is defined by:
Consistent, nurturing relationships give children the confidence to explore and the security to learn – an idea echoed by both research and wider public discourse.
At Radnor House, these elements are intentional - embedded in every interaction, activity and space, designed to support both emotional security and intellectual curiosity.
From Pre-School to Reception and Beyond
One of the most common questions parents ask is: What does it mean to be “school ready”?
It is not about early academic pressure. True readiness is the ability to:
These capabilities are developed through play, structure and relationships - not acceleration. When these foundations are secure, academic learning follows naturally.
A Foundation for Life
There is a reason it is called the foundation stage. Like the foundations of a building, it is rarely visible but determines everything that follows.
A strong early years experience shapes:
There is growing recognition across research and society that these early experiences have lifelong consequences. At Radnor House, we see this every day. Children who begin in a nurturing, stimulating environment carry forward confidence, curiosity and a genuine love of learning.
Our pre-school is built on a simple belief: every child deserves the strongest possible start.
It is an approach grounded in both the science of development and the importance of human connection.
The early years pass quickly, but their impact lasts a lifetime. By five, much of the groundwork is already in place. A high-quality early years education does not simply prepare children for school - it gives them the confidence, capability and curiosity to thrive far beyond it.
At Radnor, Deputy Head Academic (Prep) and Head of Early Years, Faye Green reflects “The early years are often described as preparation for school, but they are where everything begins. By the time a child reaches Reception, so much of their confidence, curiosity and capacity to learn has already been shaped. Our role is to nurture those qualities through meaningful relationships, rich experiences and a genuine understanding of each individual child.”

Pastoral Care | Senior | Radnor House Sevenoaks | Private School in Kent
Pupil Welfare and Support at Radnor
At Radnor, the welfare of our pupils is paramount.
We strive to create a happy, secure, and active learning environment where every student feels welcomed, supported, and valued. Our dedicated community of teachers and support staff work tirelessly to cater to each pupil as an individual, ensuring they can enjoy their education and thrive.
Our commitment to welfare extends to our staff, parents, and visitors. We aim to make everyone feel accepted for who they are, celebrated for their strengths, and supported to grow in areas of weakness. With small class sizes, extensive co-curricular opportunities, and a values-based ethos, we provide outstanding pastoral care, ensuring pupils always have someone to turn to and someone looking out for them.
It Takes A Village: How School Communities Can Transform Mental Health
How to Let Go: Supporting Children Through New Beginnings
In Conversations With: Kevin Hanley - The Kind Of Men We Want To Raise
Comprehensive Support System
Support for pupils is ingrained in every aspect of their school lives. We work in partnership with families to create opportunities and maintain the structures necessary for pupils to achieve their best. Our goal is to develop fulfilled, successful, and happy children who leave Radnor as confident young adults.
Support Network
Support and guidance are available from all staff members. The class teacher in the Prep School and Form Tutor in the Senior School are the first points of contact. Other pastoral leaders, including Deputy Heads, Heads of School, the Head of Student Support, play significant roles in pupil support. We offer confidential support for any pupil who wishes to discuss anxieties or concerns.
House System
Upon joining Radnor, pupils and staff are placed in one of our four Houses: Hever Hawks, Penshurst Falcons, Lullingstone Kites, and Eynsford Eagles. They remain in their House throughout their time at Radnor, competing in inter-House sports and cultural competitions and collaborating to raise money for their House charities.
Rewards and Sanctions
Our reward and sanction system encourages pupils to embody our core values and achieve their full potential. In the Prep School, we use a Class Dojo points system from Reception to Year 6, with pupils recognized in weekly Celebration Assemblies. Points contribute to House totals, with the House Cup awarded at the end of the academic year.
For Senior School pupils, high standards of behaviour and respect are expected in all activities. They are given numerous opportunities to find success and be celebrated, whether in a club, the classroom, or on the sports field. At the beginning of each academic year, all pupils and their parents sign a Behaviour Agreement to show their support for the school's behaviour policy.

Nursery Pastoral Care | Nursery and Pre-School | Radnor House Sevenoaks | Private School in Kent
Pastoral Care
At the heart of our Pre School is the belief that happy children are eager learners.
We are deeply committed to providing a warm, caring environment where every child feels valued, engaged, and supported. Our aim is to inspire a life-long love of learning through experiences that challenge, nurture, and build confidence.
Guided by the core values of courage, respect, perseverance, and excellence, we work hand in hand with families to create a strong foundation for your child's future. We take pride in offering not only academic excellence but also a personalised approach to pastoral care that focuses on each child's well-being and emotional development. This ensures that from their earliest days with us, your child is prepared to grow into a confident, successful global citizen.
Our class sizes reflect our philosophy of individualised care and attention. With high adult-to-child ratios, we can offer an exceptional level of personal, social, and academic growth for every child. This close-knit, nurturing environment provides the “home away from home” feeling that children need to thrive.
Our carefully designed indoor and outdoor learning spaces encourage purposeful, adaptive learning experiences, both adult-led and child-initiated. This balance fosters confidence, independence, and creativity, while supporting the development of key life skills, including working memory, flexible thinking, and inhibitory control—the cornerstones of executive function.
By providing this holistic support, we ensure that your child embarks on their learning journey with a sense of joy, belonging, and readiness for the exciting world ahead.

Nursery Curriculum | Nursery and Pre-School | Radnor House Sevenoaks | Private School in Kent
Nurturing Confident, Happy Learners
At our Pre School, we embrace a child-centred curriculum that recognises every child as a unique individual.
Learning is guided by the Radnor Archway Curriculum, our distinctive educational framework that gives children a rich, well-rounded start to their education while also nurturing vital personal and social skills. From making choices and taking initiative, to dressing themselves or selecting activities, children are encouraged to develop independence, confidence, and a love of learning.
Through tailored daily planning, we meet the developmental needs of each child whilst adhering to the UK Government’s Early Years Foundation Stage Framework, covering essential areas such as:
The Radnor Archway Curriculum is a caring and imaginative approach to learning, designed to help every child grow in confidence, curiosity and joy, from their very first days in Nursery through to Sixth Form.
In our Preschool, learning is playful, purposeful and full of wonder. Children explore ideas through stories, songs, movement, creativity and hands-on experiences that spark their natural curiosity. Rather than learning in isolated subjects, we gently connect learning together, helping children make sense of the world around them in a way that feels exciting and meaningful.
Our approach nurtures the whole child. Alongside early language, number and creative skills, we place great importance on social development, emotional wellbeing and building positive relationships. Children are encouraged to ask questions, share ideas, solve problems and develop independence — all within a warm, supportive environment where they feel safe and valued.
At Radnor, education is about more than early academic foundations. It is about helping children develop confidence, kindness and a love of learning that will stay with them for life, preparing them not just for school, but for the world beyond it.
Radnor Archway Curriculum
Personal, Social, and Emotional Development
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World
Specialist Teaching
What truly sets our curriculum apart is the depth added through specialist teaching across a wide range of subjects. Throughout the week, children benefit from engaging, immersive lessons led by experienced subject specialists in areas such as:
We believe in fostering a strong connection to the wider school community, helping children make a seamless transition to Reception. They take part in school-wide events such as the Nativity play, swimming gala, and Sports Day — each offering valuable opportunities to build confidence, celebrate achievements, and develop a sense of belonging.
SPECIALIST TEACHING AREAS
We believe in the transformative power of the performing arts, guided by our philosophy of Performance for All. Each week, Pre-School children take part in dedicated drama and music lessons led by a specialist. These sessions are designed to complement and reinforce the themes explored in the classroom, while also developing essential skills such as imagination, teamwork and confidence. Each year, our Nursery children perform in a heart-warming Nativity, giving every child the opportunity to shine, build confidence and celebrate their creativity in front of a live audience.
French lessons take place once a week in our Nursery, in small, supportive groups. The focus is on fun, fostering a love of language from an early age. Children learn French through songs, puppets, games, stories, and creative activities, with each lesson carefully planned to be varied, engaging, and full of discovery. Weekly photos on Tapestry keep families connected to their child’s learning, and our topics are closely linked to the Archway Curriculum for a seamless approach to learning. The highlight of the year is our lively French concert in the summer term, where parents are always delighted by the progress their children have made!
Physical development is a key part of life at Nursery. PE sessions take place weekly in small groups, focusing on developing balance, coordination, and agility through games, movement, and simple challenges. Lessons are designed to be fun and inclusive, helping children build confidence, teamwork and resilience.
Swimming lessons in our 25-metre indoor pool, give children the chance to develop water confidence and basic swimming skills in a safe and supportive environment. Lessons are tailored to each child’s ability and delivered by experienced instructors, combining fun activities with essential water safety skills.
Forest School is a weekly adventure for our Nursery children, taking place in our inspiring outdoor learning areas. Guided by our qualified Forest School leader, children explore nature, take managed risks, and develop independence through a wide range of hands-on activities, from building and bug discovery to creative play and imaginative challenges. Each session is designed to foster a deep connection with the natural world, while enhancing essential life skills, resilience, confidence and a sense of curiosity
Every week, our Nursery children enjoy a visit to the Prep School library, where they explore a world of stories and imagination. They choose books to enjoy independently or share in group storytime, helping to develop early literacy skills, a love of reading, and confidence in handling books. Library time also encourages curiosity, language development, and social interaction, forming an important part of our Archway Curriculum and the children’s early learning journey.
Beyond the classroom, nursery children can experience co-curricular activities such as dance, tennis and Taekwon-Do.

Inspection Reports | Radnor House Sevenoaks | Private School in Kent
Inspection Reports
ISI Inspection - November 2025
In November 2025, Radnor House Sevenoaks was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) under the current inspection framework.
This inspection evaluated the extent to which the school meets the Independent School Standards across five key areas, including leadership and management, quality of education, pupil wellbeing and safeguarding.
All inspection standards were met across every area.
In addition, the inspectors identified a significant strength in the way leaders and staff foster pupils’ individuality and listen carefully to pupils’ views. This recognition is awarded sparingly under the ISI framework and reflects practice judged to have a clear, demonstrable and highly beneficial impact on pupils.
The inspectors noted that pupils’ voices are embedded meaningfully across school life and that this approach substantially develops pupils’ confidence, self-esteem and sense of responsibility towards others.
ISI Inspection Highlights 2025
Our ISI Inspection Highlights Report offers a concise and accessible summary of our most recent inspection findings. Drawing directly on inspectors’ observations and quotations, it captures the key themes of the report and reflects what matters most to us as a school.
Download our ISI Inspection Highlights Report to find out more.
Focused Compliance Inspection (FCI) - April 2022
In April 2022, Radnor House Sevenoaks underwent a Focused Compliance Inspection (FCI) conducted by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI). This inspection reviewed various school policies and procedures, including curriculum, health and safety, recruitment, safeguarding, and leadership. The inspection's purpose was to ensure that the school complies with the Independent Schools Standards Regulations.
Outcome: The school met the standards in all eight discrete areas, which is the highest possible achievement under the current inspection framework.
Educational Quality Inspection (EQI)- April 2022
Alongside the FCI, the ISI also conducted an Educational Quality Inspection (EQI), which evaluated the school's performance in two key areas: "pupils' academic and other achievements" and "pupils' personal development." Each of these areas includes eight standards against which the school's performance is measured.
These ratings reflect the school's strong commitment to providing high-quality education and fostering personal growth among students.
Pupils' Personal Development: Rated as "Good"
Regulatory Compliance Inspection (RCI) - March 2018
In March 2018, Radnor House Sevenoaks was reviewed by the ISI in a Regulatory Compliance Inspection (RCI). This inspection covered all sections of the school, from the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) to the Sixth Form.
Outcome: The school met the standards in all eight discrete areas, marking the highest possible achievement under this inspection framework. The RCI confirmed that Radnor House Sevenoaks was fully compliant with the significant legislative requirements, including curriculum, health and safety, recruitment, safeguarding, and governance.

Academic Excellence
Radnor House Sevenoaks is a hub of academic aspiration where we expect and achieve excellence for each pupil through small class sizes and outstanding teaching.
Our students have access to a diverse curriculum, spanning from core subjects like maths and English to the arts, including drama and computing. We take immense pride in our students’ achievements, which reflect not only their hard work and dedication but also the exceptional quality of our teaching staff who inspire every student to reach their full potential.
We know each pupil well and support their development in self-knowledge and self-belief, enabling them to become adept at self-reflection and goal setting. Our students are given the time and opportunities to broaden their intellectual horizons, develop their critical thinking, ask bigger questions, and find better answers.
Read about Academic Excellence at Radnor in our latest December update.
Lower School (Years 7 and 8)
In the Lower School, students follow a broad and balanced curriculum focused on skill development, knowledge acquisition, confidence building, and striving for excellence. They study French and Spanish, along with core subjects such as maths, English, biology, chemistry, physics, computing, religious education, music, geography, history, art, and drama. Literacy is promoted through dedicated Library time with our Director of Reading and Literature to ensure all students develop high-level language and literacy skills and a love of reading.
Our extensive enrichment program includes visiting specialists, speakers, trips, theatre visits, and internal events like our Poetry Slam and Oracy Day. PE, swimming, and outdoor education are also part of the weekly timetable, as we believe physical activity is crucial for all students.
Middle School (Years 9, 10 and 11)
The Key Stage 3 curriculum concludes at the end of the Year 9 Spring Term with examinations immediately after Easter, leading to the commencement of GCSE studies. Students at Radnor House are expected to study ten GCSE subjects. Six subjects are compulsory, with a further four chosen as optional subjects, allowing students to tailor part of their curriculum to their interests and strengths.
During the Autumn Term of Year 9, students prepare for GCSE options through “taster” lessons, dedicated careers guidance sessions, and a Q&A options assembly with Sixth Form students. Option blocks are then distributed, enabling students to make their selections. The Spring Term includes a parents’ evening to discuss options with teachers, and final choices are submitted in early February of Year 9.
All students take a core programme of compulsory GCSE subjects, alongside four optional subjects selected from the options blocks.

Sport at Radnor House
Participation in sports is a fundamental part of the educational experience at Radnor House Sevenoaks, embodying our core values.
At Radnor House Sevenoaks, sport is for everyone. Whether your child already loves competition or is still finding the activity that feels right, our programme is designed to build confidence, fitness and enjoyment - while teaching teamwork, respect and resilience through shared experiences.
We celebrate every individual’s sporting journey. That means broad choice, skilled coaching and a curriculum that prioritises foundations as well as performance. From learning key movement skills and reintroducing fundamentals such as gymnastics, to representing the school in weekly fixtures, pupils are supported to develop at their own pace - and to discover what they are capable of.
Our approach: Participation and Personal Development
Sport at Radnor is not only about taking part. We develop pupils as sporting people: leadership, communication, decision-making and responsibility. Alongside playing, pupils can explore pathways such as officiating/umpiring, coaching and life-saving qualifications (e.g. NPLQ), with tangible milestones like awards and certificates recognising progress and commitment.

Sixth Form Sport: Choice, Fitness and Lifelong Habits
In Sixth Form, students have one Games afternoon per week, designed to support wellbeing and build sustainable habits alongside academic study. Options include:
This blend of competitive and recreational opportunities allows every student - from team players to those focused on personal fitness - to stay active in a way that works for them along with their academic studies.
“There’s a clear pathway if you want to take sport seriously - training, analysis, fixtures but it’s balanced with the idea that sport should be enjoyable.The standard is high, but the environment is positive.”
A through-school sporting journey: Prep to Senior
Our sporting philosophy is joined up across the school: building a lifelong love of activity in Prep, then developing skill, confidence and game understanding in Senior.
In Prep, pupils experience a broad range including cross country, basketball, tennis, dance, gymnastics, football, hockey and netball/rugby, with swimming taught separately once per week and short blocks such as table tennis. As pupils progress into the Senior School, the focus expands to include tactical understanding, performance under pressure, and the values of winning and losing well - all underpinned by respect and strong relationships.

Revision, Rest and Retrieval: Making the Most of Study Leave | Blog | Radnor House Sevenoaks | Private School in Kent
Revision, Rest and Retrieval: Making the Most of Study Leave
As study leave begins, it can be tempting for students to measure success by the number of hours spent at a desk. However, the students who use this time most effectively understand a simple truth: it is not the number of hours that matters, but how those hours are used.
The brain learns best through active retrieval - testing knowledge, applying it and explaining it - rather than simply re-reading notes. Research consistently shows that spaced retrieval practice is far more effective for long-term memory than passive revision techniques such as highlighting or repeatedly reading over material. Effective revision strategies might include completing past papers under timed conditions, using flashcards to test key knowledge, or “blurting” everything remembered onto a page before checking for gaps.
One of the most powerful ways to strengthen memory recall is to teach someone else. Explaining ideas helps to deepen understanding and identify areas that need further attention. Whether that is a parent, sibling, friend or even a pet, the important part is the process of retrieving and articulating knowledge.
A well-structured study leave can also significantly reduce stress by giving students a sense of control. Having a clear plan for each day or week removes uncertainty and helps maintain focus. Many students benefit from working in focused blocks of 60 to 90 minutes, although this will naturally vary depending on attention span and learning style.
Structuring the day in a similar way to the school timetable - with a consistent start time, regular breaks and healthy sleep patterns - helps students work when their brains are most alert, while also mirroring the timing and rhythm of exams themselves.
One of the greatest challenges during study leave can be managing distraction. Phones and social media can quickly interrupt focus, so creating device-free study periods or using app blockers can help students maintain concentration and work more effectively.
There will inevitably be moments when students “hit a wall”. At those points, the most effective response is often not to push harder, but to step away and reset. A walk, stretching, listening to music or even a burst of movement can help clear the mind and improve focus. Physical activity increases endorphins and dopamine, helping to lift mood, reduce stress and restore mental energy. Many students discover during study leave that shorter, focused revision sessions are often far more productive than trying to study continuously for hours at a time.
Social connection is equally important. Taking well-earned breaks with family or friends can provide valuable perspective and emotional balance, reminding students that while exams matter, they do not define them.
Parents also play a crucial role throughout exam season. The most supportive approach is often to remain calm and consistent - offering encouragement, maintaining routines and ensuring students are eating and resting well. Creating a steady, reassuring environment allows young people to focus without unnecessary pressure.
It is also important for students to recognise that difficult revision sessions or disappointing practice results are a normal part of the learning process. Progress is rarely linear, and confidence often grows through persistence rather than immediate success.
At Radnor, we often remind students that exams are a marathon, not a sprint. Success is not about perfection, but perseverance under pressure. It comes from pacing yourself, resting when needed, fuelling your body well and drawing on the support of those around you.
What matters most is crossing the finish line with resilience, confidence and the knowledge that you have given it your very best.
Ultimately, study leave is not simply about preparing for exams, but about developing the independence, resilience and self-management skills that students will carry with them far beyond the exam hall.
Trish Read
Head of Sixth Form and Psychology
